content: 1. The term Saturation Index refers to a mathematical representation or scale that indicates the ability of water to either deposit calcium carbonate or dissolve materials such as metal, concrete, or grout. 2. Secondary Disinfection Systems are additional disinfection processes or systems installed beyond the standard systems required for all aquatic venues. These are specifically mandated for aquatic venues with increased risk. 3. A Shower is a device designed to spray water onto the body. 4. A Cleansing Shower is a shower located within a hygiene facility that uses warm water and soap. Its purpose is to remove contaminants such as perianal fecal material, sweat, skin cells, personal care products, and dirt before bathers enter the aquatic venue. 5. A Rinse Shower is typically located in the pool deck area and uses ambient temperature water. Its primary purpose is to remove dirt, sand, or organic material before entering the aquatic venue, thereby reducing the introduction of contaminants and the formation of disinfection by-products. 6. A Skimmer is a device installed in the pool wall to remove floating debris and surface water, directing it to the filtration system. It includes a weir to automatically adjust to small changes in water level, ensuring continuous skimming of surface water. 7. A Skimmer System refers to periodic locations along the top of the pool wall designed to remove water from the pool's surface for treatment. 8. A Slide is an aquatic feature that allows users to slide down from an elevated height into the water. 9. A Drop Slide is a type of slide that drops bathers into the water from a height above the water, rather than delivering them to a water entry point. 10. A Pool Slide is a slide configured as defined in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Title 16, Part 1207 by the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), or similar in construction to a playground slide, allowing users to slide from an elevated height into a pool. This includes children's (tot) slides and other non-flume slides mounted on the pool deck or within the basin of a public swimming pool. 11. A Waterslide is a slide that terminates into a landing pool or runout through a fabricated channel with flowing water. 12. Sound Absorption refers to (1) the process of dissipating sound energy and (2) the property of materials, objects, or structures, such as rooms, to absorb sound energy. 13. Superchlorination involves the addition of large quantities of chlorine-based chemicals to kill algae, eliminate odors, or improve the ability to maintain a disinfectant residual. This process differs from hyperchlorination, which involves a prescribed amount to achieve a specific CT inactivation value, whereas superchlorination raises free chlorine levels for water quality maintenance. 14. Supplemental Treatment Systems are disinfection processes or systems not required for health and safety reasons in an aquatic venue. They may be used to enhance overall system performance and improve water quality. 15. Theoretical Peak Occupancy refers to the anticipated peak number of bathers in an aquatic venue or the anticipated peak number of occupants on the decks of an aquatic facility. This value is used for design purposes to determine services that support occupants. 16. Flat Water describes an aquatic venue where the water line remains static except for movement caused by users, typically in horizontal use such as swimming. Diving spargers do not void the flat water definition. 17. Agitated Water refers to an aquatic venue with mechanical means (aquatic features) to discharge, spray, or move the water's surface above and/or below the static water line, allowing people to stand or play vertically. If there is no static water line, movement is considered above the deck plane. 18. Hot Water describes an aquatic venue with a water temperature exceeding 90°F (32°C). 19. Turnover or Turnover Rate or Turnover Time refers to the period, usually expressed in hours, required to circulate a volume of water equal to the capacity of the aquatic venue. 20. An Underwater Bench is a submerged seat, which may or may not include hydrotherapy jets. 21. An Underwater Ledge or Underwater Toe Ledge is a continuous step in the pool wall that allows swimmers to rest by standing without treading water. 22. A Zero Depth Entry is a sloped entry into a pool from deck level into the interior of the pool, providing a means of access and egress. 23. Handrails in aquatic venues must be constructed of corrosion-resistant materials and securely anchored. The upper railing surface of handrails must extend above the pool coping or deck by a minimum of 28 inches (71.1 cm).
